How to read common Welsh digraphs without overforcing them

Dd sounds like an English "th" but softer—like the difference between "this" and "that." It's not two separate letters; treat it as one unit. Ll has no English equivalent. Think of it as an L with breath behind it, almost like saying "cll" quickly. Neither digraph should be parsed letter-by-letter on the board.

Players who treat dd as two distinct slots waste guesses fast. The board marks each position independently, so a correct dd placement gives you feedback on both squares—but only if you've actually placed that digraph. Guessing single D's near a confirmed dd rarely helps.

The instinct to eliminate letters based on English rarity kills solves here. When the board shows yellow on Y, don't assume it's a fluke. Welsh words use Y as a primary vowel in many syllables. Similarly, starting a guess with W isn't wasteful—it's often the right move.
